chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Sinan, from one of his companions, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no greater army for Iblees than women and anger.'
ai.seo_question: What are the two greatest armies of Iblees according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith, found in al-Kafi's chapter on the scarcity of righteousness among women, identifies women and anger as the two greatest 'armies' of Iblees, emphasizing their dual role in spiritual vulnerability. In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted not as a general贬低 of women, but as a specific reference to their influence on men's emotional states and the potent combination of feminine allure and male wrath in leading to sin. The narration underscores the need for self-regulation of anger and mindfulness in marital and social interactions to counteract these forces.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Sinan, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘There is no greater army for Iblees<sup>la</sup> than the women and the anger’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ’Isa from ibn Mahbub from ibn Sinan from certain persons of his people who have said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘
No other thing serves Satan as the greatest army as women and anger do.’”
